## Context / Problem
S1-S6 establish a shared policy and execution path across two mature gates. Unit coverage inside each story is necessary but cannot prove that the combined default path uses one policy authority, makes no duplicate shadow calls, preserves narrow outputs, survives the real provider boundary, or remains centralized after later edits. RP-06 therefore needs a permanent cross-gate cutover guard and live exercise.

## Approach
Add a deterministic shadow comparator that consumes the same observed call/result set as the legacy and RP-06 projections. Compare criterion selection and exclusion, order, prompt/contract identity, context hash, model/mode, dependencies, budgets, posture, usage, checkpoint decisions, and final disposition. Its allowlist names only the approved deltas: effective built-in retune/disable, project DET inclusion, project LLM applicability, positive code-review budget enforcement, typed partial-failure continuation, and success-only checkpointing. Shadowing never issues a model call and never controls the final verdict.

Add a repository-policy/contract guard that fails when a review gate bypasses `CriteriaSnapshot` to read packaged/project routing directly, when a second discovery scheduler is introduced outside the shared kernel, or when per-unit trace fields enter review/review-status schemas. Use semantic imports/contracts where possible and a narrowly scoped AST/source policy only for the prohibited direct-reader pattern.

Exercise both defaulted gate paths through the existing external LLM provider matrix. The canary uses real workflow dispatch and a minimal bounded fixture, proves at least one discovery call reaches the configured provider, and asserts the final narrow verdict plus stored internal trace. It must not print secrets, raw prompt/context bodies, or the trace. Record the provider arm, run URL, timestamp, call count, and result on this ticket.

Document the final ownership and rollback boundary in `docs/review-kernel.md`: authored topology and gate strategy remain gate-owned; snapshot and execution facts are shared; RP-01 owns provider-turn retry; rollback is a code revert to the retained compatibility projection, not an operator configuration flag. New code ignores legacy checkpoints and the retained legacy projection never writes the new journal.

## Testing
The deterministic comparator and architecture guard run in the normal unit/repository-policy gate. Response-schema tests assert exact public keys. The live canary lives under `tests/external/`, carries the existing `external` and `llm_live` confinement, and is selected by the configured provider matrix. One tier lower cannot prove the provider/workflow cutover because a fake can bypass the default runtime path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The shadow comparator uses one observed call set, emits no provider calls, and reports exact field-level mismatches with only the approved delta allowlist accepted.
- [x] Cross-gate fixtures for no overlay, effective disable/retune, scoped/global project LLM, project DET, budget shed, local failure, systemic failure, cancellation, and legacy checkpoint produce the approved final dispositions and trace outcomes.
- [x] A repository-policy/contract test fails on direct gate reads that bypass `CriteriaSnapshot`, a second discovery scheduler outside the shared kernel, or per-unit trace/debug fields added to review or review-status output schemas.
- [x] Public response-schema tests prove `review-plan`, `review-plan --status`, and code-review outputs remain narrow while their reducer-ignored journals retain versioned internal traces.
- [x] New code ignores legacy checkpoint envelopes, the retained compatibility projection cannot write new envelopes or decide a final verdict, and a revert to that projection requires no journal rewrite or data cleanup.
- [x] `docs/review-kernel.md` states final snapshot/executor/gate/RP-01 ownership, approved deltas, sensitive-data boundary, shadow behavior, and revert-based rollback.
- [x] A live provider canary at `tests/external/test_review_discovery_live.py`, confined to the `external`+`llm_live` markers and selected by the provider matrix, drives the real default discovery path and asserts a narrow final verdict (PASS/BLOCK) with `coverage.llm_ran` true and the reducer-ignored internal journal retained (`sidecar_emitted`), printing no secrets, prompt/context bodies, or trace.
- [x] [operator-attested] The external provider matrix run exercised that real default plan-review/code-review discovery path against live providers, recorded at least one provider call per exercised arm, and this ticket records provider, run URL, timestamp, call count, and final result.
  provenance: environment=external-provider-matrix; principal=configured CI workload identity; privilege_posture=provider-scoped; instrument=`pytest -m "external and llm_live"` selected by the provider matrix — the run URL and per-provider result are attached to this ticket.
